title: Evaluator grammar, naming and robustness fixes

features.notes: Accept only the calculator grammar. Before the sympy parse, run a token/grammar check that rejects Python comparison, %, //, bitwise and shift operators, hex/bin/oct/underscore/j literals, and extra arguments to unary functions. Keep 5!, := and implied multiplication working. Add a unittest for each listed input.

Treat a multi-letter identifier as one symbol. Drop letter splitting and map only known names (pi, e, function names). E, I, S, N, Q and similar names become plain Symbols. Keep 2x, 2pi and 2sin(...) working. Share the tokenizer with P23.
Decimal formatting only. Past 12 digits, use scientific notation with 12 significant digits and no trailing zeros, e.g. 1.26765060023e30. Existing decimal tests must still pass.

Store ans, variables and functions as sympy objects or in a form that parses again, so names like beta, zeta, gamma, S, N and Q never break a later evaluation. ans must give back the same exact string. Builds on P24. Add a regression test for each listed sequence.
